label: churn200-s0
summary: The churn model adds its parts on the logit scale and passes the sum through a sigmoid; the annotated structure reproduces it to 3.3e-16 on every training row, and its training AUC is 0.924. Three routes lead to high predicted churn. First, customer-service calls: two gates add risk once a customer has called several times, sooner for light daytime users; of the 318 training customers with four or more calls, 50% churned. Second, a high daytime bill without voicemail messages, the most important single part: switching it off lowers training AUC to 0.740; it acts on 661 customers whose observed churn rate is 40.4%. Third, an international plan (typical-customer risk 65% against 12% without) and a high international charge. A voicemail plan lowers risk. State offsets, a long-account hinge and small usage terms adjust the rest; the state offsets are fitted to small groups of customers. The model over-predicts on average: mean predicted risk 34% against an observed churn rate of 14.1%.
